name: Assisted living / memory care
summary: Licensed assisted living with a secured memory-care wing: small private units (~350-550 SF), large dining/activity/care common areas, commercial kitchen, nurse call, wander management, generator and institutional-grade fire protection. Per-SF cost runs ~20% above independent living (Weitz 2025-26), and per bed it depends on gross SF per bed. Per-SF data are national survey ranges; per-bed figures are derived, with one older project as a check. Memory-care-specific cost data were not found publicly.

typicalSize.method: Typical stand-alone AL/MC building 60-80 AL + 20-32 MC units; Fairfield County example 90 AL + 40 MC units (e3). Beds ~1.05-1.1x units (companion suites).

sfPerPrimaryUnit.method: Gross SF per bed: AL units ~450-550 net SF and MC units ~300-375 net SF; common/care/dining/kitchen/corridors take ~40-50% of gross => AL ~850-950, MC ~650-750 GSF per bed; blended ~800.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Single- or two-story suburban AL/MC ~15-30 beds/acre; three-story and urban projects higher (judgment).

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Few residents drive; parking serves staff shifts and visitors - typically 0.4-0.75 spaces per bed (judgment; local code governs).

perPrimaryUnit.method: Derived: perSF x sfPerPrimaryUnit: mid $320 x 800 = $256k (rounded $255k); low $280 x 700 = $196k; high $400 x 950 = $380k. Check: Fairfield County CT 2020 AL/MC ~$290k/unit (e3; low confidence, scope unclear, older dollars).

perSF.method: Weitz 2026 mid-level AL $280-356 (midpoint $318) and high-level $363-452 (e1); April 2025 mid-level $278-354 (e2). Mid $320 = mid-level midpoint; low = bottom of mid-level; high ~ middle of high-level range (luxury tier extends further). Memory care is assumed at the AL rate per SF (secure courtyards and higher common-area share show up in SF per bed rather than $/SF).

scope.notes: Contractor price incl. general conditions, OH&P, commercial kitchen and laundry equipment, nurse call, generator, secured courtyard and on-site work; excludes land, soft costs, FF&E, off-sites, impact fees, financing, licensing and pre-opening. Weitz does not state whether its ranges include sitework - verify.

qualityTiers.method: Weitz high-level vs mid-level AL midpoints: $407.5 / $318 = 1.28 (e1) sets premium ~1.25; economy = bottom of mid-level ($280/$318 = 0.88); luxury by judgment.

systemSplit.method: Derived from the independent-living split in this category: +1.5 pts HVAC (23, PTAC/VRF per unit plus kitchen/laundry exhaust, care-area ventilation), +1.0 pt plumbing (22, accessible showers, assisted bathing, laundry), +0.5 pt electrical (26, generator), +0.4 pt each nurse call (27) and wander management/fire alarm (28), +0.3 pt sprinklers (21, I-2/I-1 occupancy), +0.2 pt specialties (10, grab bars); offset by less concrete (-1.5, mostly 1-3 stories on grade), framing, finishes, casework and elevators; 01 absorbs rounding.

lineItems.name: Commercial kitchen, servery and central laundry

cost.method: Derived: institutional kitchen with hoods, walk-ins, dish and central laundry for ~100 beds (2026 judgment).

lineItems.name: Nurse call and wander-management / access control

cost.method: Derived: UL 1069 / wireless nurse call with locating and secured-unit door controls (2026 judgment).

lineItems.name: Emergency generator (life safety + resident comfort loads)

cost.method: Derived: 300-750 kW diesel/natural gas set with ATS; several states now require backup power for AL temperature control (2026 judgment).

lineItems.name: Secured memory-care courtyard and wandering path

cost.method: Derived: fenced courtyard, looped path, shade, lighting and landscaping (2026 judgment).

perPrimaryUnit.method: Derived: common-area furniture, dining, activity, therapy/wellness, kitchen smallwares and furnished MC rooms ~ $1.0-2.2M for ~100 beds (2026 judgment). Operator-specific; verify.

pctOfHard.method: Derived: RAND multifamily soft/hard 0.19-0.33 incl. financing (e5) plus healthcare-specific items (licensing/CON consultants, operator technical services, life-safety/state health plan review); mid 0.28 excluding construction interest and operating pre-opening.

softCosts.notes: Model pre-opening (staffing, training, marketing) and operating-deficit reserves separately; certificate-of-need states add application costs and time.

design.method: Derived industry norm for licensed healthcare-adjacent buildings.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Hard low $195k x 1.15 ~= $225k; hard high $380k x 1.48 ~= $560k.

source.title: Assisted Living Construction Costs Rise in 2026, Independent Living Costs Remain Flat (Feb 3, 2026; Weitz 'Senior Living Construction Costs' report)

evidence.quote: Mid-level assisted living projects cost between $280 and $356 ... High level assisted living construction costs remain the same since August at a range of $363 to $452 per square foot.
evidence.scopeNotes: Weitz 'Senior Living Construction Costs' report (early 2026) via SHN; memory care not separately reported; scope (sitework, FF&E) not stated.

source.title: Senior Living Construction Costs Could Rise 4% to 6% in Next 12 Months (Apr 21, 2025; Weitz construction costs brief)

evidence.quote: Assisted living projects range in cost from $278 to $354 per square foot
evidence.scopeNotes: Weitz April 2025 brief, mid-level assisted living, via SHN.

source.title: Carnegie Capital closes Fairfield County construction loan (Dec 27, 2020)

evidence.quote: 90 assisted living and 40 memory care units ... that puts the construction cost at nearly $37.7 million ... The five-year construction loan totaled $24.5 million
evidence.scopeNotes: One AL/MC project (130 units), 2020; ~$290k/unit. The 'construction cost' appears to be inferred from the loan and may be total project cost; scope unclear.

source.title: Assisted Living Construction Costs Rise in 2026, Independent Living Costs Remain Flat (Feb 3, 2026; Weitz 'Senior Living Construction Costs' report)

evidence.quote: Costs of mid-level independent living projects registered between $240 and $292 per square foot
evidence.scopeNotes: IL comparison from the same Weitz survey - AL mid-level runs ~17-22% above IL per SF.

source.title: The High Cost of Producing Multifamily Housing in California (RAND RR-A3743-1, Ward & Schlake, 2025) - copy hosted by San Diego Housing Commission

evidence.quote: Table 3.1 Panel C. Soft Costs: Texas Market rate $22; Colorado Market rate $44; California Market rate $84 (vs Panel A hard costs $115 / $237 / $253 per NRSF)
evidence.scopeNotes: Soft/hard ratios derived: TX 0.19, CO 0.19, CA 0.33. RAND soft costs include A&E, legal, fees and financing costs; market-rate sample mixes garden, podium, wrap, high-rise.

openQuestions: Memory-care-specific $/SF and GSF per bed (state CON filings, e.g., NC/KY/GA, list project cost, beds and SF) would sharpen the mid and allow a separate MC adjustment.
Weitz scope (sitework/FF&E) is not stated in the public summaries.
Kitchen, nurse call, generator and courtyard items are derived.
